list_entry.title: Letter to the editor: Sites are needed for disposal

A.explanation:
We don't hear anything about the editor's view other than "your approach". It's hard to distort someone's view if you just say "your view".

This answer refers to a famous flaw called Straw Man. It would feel more like Person A saying "I think we should install solar panels on the roof" and Person B saying, "Well, I'm not so sure we should be spending all the company's money on green initiatives".

B.explanation: The conclusion is only about whether this approach would or wouldn't damage commercial fishing operations. The author is under no burden to argue that the other approach is viable or even preferable.

C.explanation:
We don't know anything about this writer so there's no way for us to say that this letter is in the writer's self-interest.

Also, it's not inherently bad to make an argument out of self-interest. We don't have to be genuinely concerned with the truth to still say truthful things and argue in a logical manner.

D.explanation:
The conclusion is based on testimony: it's the testimony of 20,000 people. We have no idea who they are. They might be exiting a Whole Foods.

Do they know anything about burying contaminated dredge spoils? Do they know anything about commercial fishing operations? This answer describes the Inappropriate Appeal to someone with dubious expertise on the matter.

E.explanation:
We don't even care about the second option. The conclusion is only about whether or not the first option will damage commercial fishing operations.

This answer describes the famous flaw of False Choice.
